title: How the amplifier's fuse holder (F34) shares the battery switch's …
ask: On the battery switch's output stud, should the starter's fuse and the amplifier's fuse share one Blue Sea 2151 dual holder instead of two stacked single holders?
why: The master disconnect's output stud already carries the main feed's lug and the starter's fuse holder (P051, a Blue Sea 5191). The amplifier's fuse F34 must start at the same stud. A second holder stacked on top may not leave enough thread for the nut, and Blue Sea makes one holder with two fuses (the 2151) for exactly this. The answer sets what is in the cart (P051), how E41.02 tells you to fit it, and F34's place.
options:
(a) One Blue Sea 2151 dual MRBF terminal fuse block on the output stud instead of the two 5191s: the starter cable on one fuse, the amplifier feed on the other, one base on the stud. About the price of two 5191s (confirm at the cart). Forecloses nothing.
(b) Keep the two 5191s and stack them on the output stud as the cart has them. No change to the cart. Whether the stud has thread for the lug, two bases and the nut is only known with the parts in hand; if not, you buy (a) or (c) then.
(c) The amplifier's fuse in a surface-mount MRBF holder screwed to the bin floor, fed by a short 4 AWG lead from the output stud. One more lug on the stud, a holder, a lead and two lugs (about $10-30 more). Takes floor space in the bin.
recommend: (a), unless the 2151 costs much more than two 5191s at the cart or will not clear the battery's boot in the bin
stops: E41.02 (fitting F34's holder); P051's line in the cart; F34's place in the fuses table
